AWS Cloud WAN now supports Flow Logs
changes.detail: AWS Cloud WAN now supports VPC Flow Logs, giving you central visibility into IP traffic across your global network. Flow Logs capture detailed information for each flow, so you can understand how traffic moves across your core network without leaving your AWS Cloud WAN account. Until now, network administrators had to stitch together VPC Flow Logs from many VPCs, accounts, and Regions to see traffic across their global network. changes.title: AWS Emulator is now available for building and testing AWS applications locally
changes.detail: AWS Emulator is now available for building and testing AWS applications locally. Starting today, you can use AWS Emulator to build and test AWS applications on your computer or in your continuous integration (CI) environment. Your existing AWS SDK and CLI calls go to AWS Emulator and come back in milliseconds, so you and your coding agents can find and fix errors locally, with no deployments or AWS account required. changes.title: Google Kubernetes Engine: Feature (November 11, 2026)
changes.detail: Capacity buffers, including active and standby capacity buffers, are generally available for GKE Standard and Autopilot clusters running version 1.37.1-gke.3020000 or later. Capacity buffers let you pre-provision and optionally suspend standby compute capacity using the CapacityBuffer custom resource (autoscaling.x-k8s.io/v1beta1) to accelerate workload scaling and mitigate capacity constraints. To get started, see About capacity buffers .
